subject: Delta margin: final capacity allocation plan for HelixAI deal
messages:
From: Simon Tang <simon.tang@helixai.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixAI Procurement <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final sizing for dedicated pool — timing and buffer ask

Ethan,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We finished the internal capacity forecast and our final ask for the dedicated environment is 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs with a peak concurrency profile around 360 qps across model variants. We recognize there will be overhead for failover and burst; HelixAI would like a proposed safety buffer and a 30–60 day activation window where we can lock the capacity.

Two specific asks: 1) can Redwood place a soft hold on capacity for 45 days while legal finishes the PO, and 2) what buffer would you recommend (percent or absolute GPUs) given our mixed batch/stream workload?

Attached: draft sizing table from our infra team.

Simon
Simon Tang
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixAI
Attachments: helix-final-sizing-v3.xlsx (see referenced spreadsheet)

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Simon Tang <simon.tang@helixai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final sizing for dedicated pool — timing and buffer ask

Simon — thanks, this is helpful. I’ve looped in Monica (CS lead), Karthik (sales/allocations), and Laura (capacity ops).

Quick answers up front: we can initiate a 45-day soft hold for a portion of that footprint while legal/finance finalizes the PO; operationally we recommend a two-tier buffer: +10% for steady-state (to absorb variance) and an additional +15% reserved as burst headroom for three-day surges tied to ramp events. For your numbers that maps to roughly: 24 base -> 26 (10% round up) steady, with 4 extra GPUs tagged as burst reserve (total 30 GPUs in the allocation plan).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to confirm if the deal is on an annual reserved cadence (affects how we price the held capacity).
- Laura to confirm exact node shapes we should earmark so we don’t fragment pools (GPU type/quantization constraints).
- I’ll open an internal soft-hold ticket and attach the Helix sizing sheet so we have an audit trail.

Simon — if that buffer looks reasonable I’ll push the ticket through and we’ll notify infra to quarantine the node subset.

Best,
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final sizing for dedicated pool — timing and buffer ask

Team — cc’ing so we have allocation and commercial alignment. A few clarifications from sales:
1) Helix is targeting an annual committed contract but needs the PO to clear first (legal/finance timeline ~2–3 weeks).
2) They’ve indicated willingness to pay for held capacity at a reduced standby rate if we need to formalize the soft hold as a paid reservation.

Operational ask: Laura, can you confirm whether earmarking 30 GPUs (as Ethan proposed) is feasible across our US-west pool for the 45 day window? If feasible, please mark as a "soft quarantine" (no billing change unless Helix confirms purchase early). If not feasible, provide the nearest equivalent node mix and any fragmentation impacts we should flag to the customer (e.g., mixing A100-80GB and A10X nodes may affect latency for the larger models).

I’ll also prepare two commercial options for Simon: (A) free soft hold for 45 days with no pricing change, subject to infra approval, or (B) paid standby at 25% of monthly reserved rate to guarantee the hold independent of infra shifts.

-karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final sizing for dedicated pool — timing and buffer ask

All — worked this with infra ops. Summary:
- US-west pool has the capacity to quarantine 30 GPUs for a 45-day soft hold, but it will require reserving three contiguous racks to avoid fragmentation (prefer A100-80GB homogeneous placement).
- I’ve opened JIRA-8742 to request a soft-quarantine action and attached the Helix sizing sheet for reference. The soft-quarantine will:
  * mark nodes as "standby-reserved" in the inventory,
  * prevent new on-demand allocations from using those GPUs,
  * set an automatic release action at 45 days unless a ticket is updated.

Attachments: infra-soft-hold-ticket-8742.txt (internal ticket stub), helix-deal-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx (from customer).

Caveat: if Helix requests a paid standby we can convert the soft quarantine to a hard reservation immediately and bill pro-rata; the billing conversion is straightforward but requires a signed PO or contract amendment.

Laura Bennett
Capacity Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Simon Tang <simon.tang@helixai.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixAI Procurement <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final sizing for dedicated pool — timing and buffer ask

Ethan / Karthik — perfect, thanks for moving quickly and for the clarity. The plan to earmark 30 GPUs for a 45-day window is acceptable. Helix prefers option B (paid standby at the reduced rate) — procurement will kick the PO today and we expect the signed order within ~7 business days. Please convert the soft-quarantine to a paid standby once infra confirms the nodes (JIRA-8742).

Also attaching our signoff matrix (helix-signoff-matrix.pdf).

Simon
